evidence.claim: Articles 83 and 84 assign the president executive authority, including appointing ministers, directing the federal administration, initiating legislation, promulgating laws, issuing decrees, and vetoing bills, while limiting foreign travel without congressional authorization.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil de 1988
evidence.excerpt: Articles 83 and 84 assign the president executive authority, including appointing ministers, directing the federal administration, initiating legislation, promulgating laws, issuing decrees, and vetoing bills, while limiting foreign travel without congressional authorization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Bolsonaro's formal authority and constraints in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Formal powers do not prove how they were used in practice.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro met Putin on an official state visit to discuss strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, agriculture, defense, cybersecurity, science and technology.
evidence.title: President Jair Bolsonaro and President Vladimir Putin meet in Moscow
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro met Putin on an official state visit to discuss strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, agriculture, defense, cybersecurity, science and technology.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release dated to the visit with direct attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Exact February 2022 timing just before the invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the visit and discussion agenda.
contrary_evidence: The release frames cooperation positively and does not itself show harmful conduct.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said Brazil would remain neutral in the Russia-Ukraine war and would not take sides, adding that the conflict was not Brazil's problem.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que não toma partido na invasão russa da Ucrânia
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said Brazil would remain neutral in the Russia-Ukraine war and would not take sides, adding that the conflict was not Brazil's problem.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting republished by UOL, contemporaneous and directly attributed to Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: Neutrality can be read as restraint, but it also avoided an explicit condemnation of the invasion.

evidence.claim: Brazil said the Security Council should pursue diplomatic solutions to the Ukraine crisis and expressed grave concern about Russian military operations against Ukrainian territory.
evidence.title: Statement and Explanation of Vote by the Permanent Representative Ambassador Ronaldo Costa Filho in the Security Council Debate on the Question of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said the Security Council should pursue diplomatic solutions to the Ukraine crisis and expressed grave concern about Russian military operations against Ukrainian territory.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-ministry statement of vote and rationale from Brazil's UN mission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official Brazilian foreign-policy position under Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: This is delegation-level language, so it is not a personal Bolsonaro speech.

evidence.claim: Brazil said it had voted for the Human Rights Council commission of inquiry on Ukraine, but abstained on the General Assembly suspension vote because it wanted that independent investigation to complete first.
evidence.title: General Assembly Adopts Text to Suspend Russian Federation from Human Rights Council, Continuing Emergency Special Session on Humanitarian Crisis in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said it had voted for the Human Rights Council commission of inquiry on Ukraine, but abstained on the General Assembly suspension vote because it wanted that independent investigation to complete first.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting record with Brazil's explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazil's UN delegation under Bolsonaro's government.
contrary_evidence: Abstention can be read as procedural caution rather than full solidarity with accountability efforts.

evidence.claim: Brazil called for accountability for sexual violence and human trafficking in Ukraine and said special humanitarian visas were being granted to Ukrainians affected by the conflict.
evidence.title: Statement by the Permanent Representative of Brazil to the United Nations, Ambassador Ronaldo Costa Filho, at the UNSC meeting on Ukraine - June 6th, 2022
evidence.excerpt: Brazil called for accountability for sexual violence and human trafficking in Ukraine and said special humanitarian visas were being granted to Ukrainians affected by the conflict.
evidence.source_locator: middle paragraphs on accountability and humanitarian visas
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-ministry archive reproducing the 2022 statement text.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 statement archived later on the ministry site.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian foreign-policy position under Bolsonaro; not a personal Bolsonaro quote.
contrary_evidence: The source is a mission statement, so it reflects official diplomacy more than direct presidential command.

evidence.claim: Brazil assumed the monthly presidency of the UN Security Council in July 2022 and the Council agenda included the Ukraine situation.
evidence.title: Presidência brasileira do Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas
evidence.excerpt: Brazil assumed the monthly presidency of the UN Security Council in July 2022 and the Council agenda included the Ukraine situation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official notice on Brazil's Council presidency and agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional role of the Brazilian government during Bolsonaro's term.
contrary_evidence: A rotating presidency is procedural power, not proof of substantive peace leadership.

evidence.claim: Brazil said the referenda in occupied Ukrainian regions escalated the conflict and called for an immediate ceasefire and the opening of peace negotiations.
evidence.title: Statement by the Permanent Representative of Brazil to the United Nations, Ambassador Ronaldo Costa Filho, at the UNSC meeting on Ukraine - September 27th, 2022
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said the referenda in occupied Ukrainian regions escalated the conflict and called for an immediate ceasefire and the opening of peace negotiations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official archived statement with explicit ceasefire language and dated 2022 text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian foreign-policy position under Bolsonaro's government.
contrary_evidence: The statement also defended self-determination language, which can soften the apparent alignment with one side.

evidence.claim: Brazil abstained on the annexation resolution, saying its calls for a cessation of hostilities and return to dialogue were not included and warning that any use of nuclear weapons would be catastrophic for humanity.
evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation’s Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
evidence.excerpt: Brazil abstained on the annexation resolution, saying its calls for a cessation of hostilities and return to dialogue were not included and warning that any use of nuclear weapons would be catastrophic for humanity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting record with Brazil's stated rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazil's UN delegation under Bolsonaro's government.
contrary_evidence: Abstention on a condemnation resolution can be read as weaker accountability than a yes vote.
